scenario: AITA for refusing an additional guest at our wedding | Thanks for watching this post. First time writing here and non-native English speaker. I am getting married very soon. As you can imagine, this takes a lot of preparation. I'm talking here about the civil wedding, which will be very intimate and consequently restricted to our very close family: parents, siblings and, in my case, godparents and their children. The wedding will happen in another country, so this takes a lot of preparation as it is in another culture. When I made the invitations, I've been clear: I invited my parents (2 p.) and my godparents' family (4 p.). I've been very flexible, I told everyone that they could join us anytime they like (i.e., arrive in the country when they wish because I understand it's complicated when you have 4 different jobs etc) as long as they'll be present for the ceremony. Moreover, because the destination is far, my in-laws kindly proposed to offer the accommodation to all of them. The wedding is now in one month and I just received a message from my godmother saying that they have booked the flights, and they will be 5 because the gf of my cousin is joining. That's where I am really feeling uncomfortable: I receive this as a 'fait accompli' (done deal) without any prior consultation, without even asking me if that's ok to have an additional person (that I've never met). I've always been clear about the number of people invited. I just can't stand to receive this kind of 'news' via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against that additional person. It's just the way that I'm put in front of this, as if I had nothing to say. And we're not talking about the 'party' wedding, but something very special that is meant to be in strict intimacy. Moreover, I know that they have their tickets since 1 month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip etc. So they literally waited 1 month to announce it, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything, and to ask if it's possible, etc. In sum, they just invited someone at my wedding, someone that wasn't ever planned and that I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: 'I'm confused by your news, I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e. you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise.' So: Am I the asshole? More precisely: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm "the asshole" in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I'm getting married soon, and I've been really clear about keeping the wedding very intimate. I only invited a few close family members: my parents, my godparents, and their children. I even told everyone they could come anytime, as long as they were there for the ceremony. Plus, my in-laws are helping with accommodation since it's in another country. Now, one month before the wedding, my godmother sends me a message saying they've booked their flights and that there will be five people instead of four because the godfather of my cousin is joining them. I'm really uncomfortable with this because they didn't ask me beforehand. I feel like they're making a decision about my wedding without consulting me, and it's presented as a done deal. I sent a polite message back, explaining that I'm confused because I've always been clear about the guest list. I asked why they didn't call me before booking anything and mentioned that this goes against what we've been planning for months. I also said that the solution doesn't lie with me, implying that I can't accept this change. Now, the question is: Am I the asshole for refusing this additional guest and for being clear about my boundaries? First, I need to consider the context. I've been clear about the guest list from the beginning. I've communicated that only specific people are invited, and I've given flexibility in terms of when they can arrive. However, adding someone new to the guest list without prior discussion seems like a breach of that agreement. I also need to think about the emotional impact. Weddings are personal events, and having an additional guest who I don't know could make the day less special and more stressful. It's understandable that I feel uncomfortable with this change, especially since it was sprung on me without any prior discussion. On the other hand, maybe my godmother and her family felt that adding someone was a small change and didn't think it would be a big deal. They might have assumed that since I was flexible with arrival times, I would also be flexible with the guest list. However, I had specifically mentioned the number of guests and the people I wanted to include, so it's reasonable that I feel this was a significant change. I also need to consider the logistics. Even though the in-laws are handling accommodation, adding another person could affect the arrangements. It's not just about the number of people but also about ensuring that everyone feels comfortable and that the day runs smoothly. In my response, I expressed my confusion and disappointment clearly. I didn't yell or blame them, but I did make it clear that I was uncomfortable with the change and that I expected to be consulted before such decisions are made. This seems like a reasonable way to communicate my feelings. However, I also need to think about whether I could have handled this differently. Maybe instead of sending a message that seemed to shut down the possibility of the additional guest, I could have expressed my concerns more gently and opened the door for further discussion. But given the time constraints and the fact that the wedding is only a month away, it's understandable that I felt the need to be firm. In conclusion, I don't think I'm "the asshole" for refusing the additional guest and for being clear about my boundaries. It's important to communicate my needs and to ensure that my wedding day reflects the plans we've made. However, I could have approached the situation with a bit more empathy and openness to discussion, even while maintaining my boundaries.
